defect: Gating the top/bottom hot zones in `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point` on `can_scroll_up`/`can_scroll_down` makes it return `None` when the user drags vertically past the top or bottom boundary of an already-pinned pane. The caller in `copy_selection.rs` assumes falling through extends the selection to the cell under the cursor via `copy_point_from_screen`, but `copy_point_from_screen` returns `None` for any row outside `content_area`, so dragging past the last or first line of a pinned pane silently stops extending the selection.
trigger: Anchor a mouse drag selection on a chat line while pinned to the bottom (so `visible_end == wrapped_plain_line_count()`), then drag the cursor vertically past the bottom of `content_area` (`row > last_row`).
match_rule: Must identify that returning `None` from `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point` when `!can_scroll_down` (or `!can_scroll_up`) causes vertical overshoot drags outside `content_area` (`row > last_row` or `row < area.y`) to fall through to `copy_point_from_screen` / `point`, which returns `None` outside the pane, so dragging past the pane edge no longer extends the selection.
near_misses: Complaining about hot-zone width, horizontal clamping, or tick-driven auto-scroll behavior when `can_scroll_down` is true; or suggesting re-enabling auto-scroll while pinned.
why_findable: The diff comment explicitly assumes returning `None` lets the caller extend selection to the cell under the cursor; checking the caller (`copy_selection.rs:517-532`) and `copy_point_from_screen` in `ui.rs` shows overshoot rows map to `None` and drop the drag update.

defect: The duplicate-driver guard in `run_swarm_plan_in_background` performs an async `manager.list().await` check for an existing running swarm driver and later spawns the driver via a separate `spawn_with_notify(...).await` call with no atomic reservation between check and spawn. Two concurrent `run_plan` calls for the same session can both pass the check before either registers its task and start duplicate drivers that race on task assignments and double-spawn workers.
trigger: Two concurrent `swarm run_plan` tool invocations for the same session (e.g., issued in the same tool batch) execute `run_swarm_plan_in_background` concurrently.
match_rule: Must identify the check-then-spawn TOCTOU race between `manager.list().await` and `spawn_with_notify(...).await` in `run_swarm_plan_in_background` allowing two concurrent `run_plan` calls for the same session to start duplicate drivers.
near_misses: Discussing stale status files after reload, `is_live_task` correctness, or task display name formatting.
why_findable: Both the `manager.list().await` duplicate check and the later `spawn_with_notify(...).await` appear right next to each other in the new `run_swarm_plan_in_background` function with no lock or claim held across the await points.

defect: `handle_mouse_event` wires the new `MouseEventKind::Up(MouseButton::Left)` inline-image expand-badge click handler (`try_cycle_image_expand_at`) after `handle_copy_selection_mouse`. On a real left click (`Down` followed by `Up`), `handle_copy_selection_mouse` arms `copy_selection_pending_anchor` on `Down` and returns `Some(false)` on `Up` whenever `had_pending` is true, short-circuiting `handle_mouse_event` before `try_cycle_image_expand_at` is ever reached.
trigger: Render an inline transcript image with an expand badge and perform a real left click (`MouseEventKind::Down(Left)` followed by `MouseEventKind::Up(Left)`) on the badge in normal mode.
match_rule: Must identify that `handle_copy_selection_mouse` runs before `try_cycle_image_expand_at` in `handle_mouse_event` and consumes the `Down`+`Up` click pair (via `copy_selection_pending_anchor` / `had_pending` returning `Some(false)` on `Up`), preventing clicks on the inline-image expand badge from ever reaching `try_cycle_image_expand_at`.
near_misses: Reporting hit-test column offset bugs inside `inline_image_expand_target_from_screen`, cache invalidation issues, or claiming `Up` alone fails.
why_findable: The commit places `try_cycle_image_expand_at` at the end of `handle_mouse_event` (its commit message even claims it is before copy), while inspecting `handle_copy_selection_mouse` called earlier in the same function shows `Down` sets `copy_selection_pending_anchor` and `Up` returns `Some(false)` whenever `had_pending` is true.

defect: `collect_recent_session_stems` pre-filters the sessions directory to the top `scan_limit` (default 300) candidates using `session_sort_key(stem)`, which parses the creation timestamp embedded in the session ID filename. Because `Session::create` sets the filename once at creation and `Session::save` updates `updated_at` in place without renaming the file, any older long-running or recently resumed session with >`scan_limit` newer-created sessions is dropped before `load_sessions` ever reads its `updated_at`.
trigger: Create an older session (low timestamp in filename), create more than `scan_limit` newer sessions, then resume and update the older session so its file mtime / `updated_at` is newest; open `/resume`.
match_rule: Must identify that `collect_recent_session_stems` ranks top-K candidates solely by the creation timestamp parsed from the session filename stem (`session_sort_key`) rather than modification time (`mtime`/`updated_at`), causing recently active sessions with older creation IDs to be evicted from the top-K scan before `load_sessions` sorts by `last_message_time`.
near_misses: Complaining about `session_sort_key` parsing 13-digit timestamps, tie-breaking on stem name, or empty stub sessions.
why_findable: `SessionSummary` in the same diff has both `created_at` and `updated_at`, `load_sessions` sorts by `last_message_time` (`updated_at`), and `src/session.rs` shows session filenames embed creation timestamps once and are never renamed on update.

defect: `MultiProvider::model_routes` adds `configured_standard_openrouter_profile_routes()` when a direct OpenAI-compatible profile owns the shared OpenRouter slot (`!supports_openrouter_provider_features && standard_openrouter_profile_configured()`), reading `load_disk_cache_entry_for_namespace("openrouter")`. However, the OpenRouter provider only writes disk cache entries for its active `configured_cache_namespace()` (the direct profile's namespace), so when a direct profile is the startup default, nothing ever populates or refreshes the `"openrouter"` cache namespace and standard OpenRouter models stay hidden in `/model`.
trigger: Configure both `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` and a direct OpenAI-compatible startup default profile (e.g. NVIDIA NIM) without a pre-existing fresh `openrouter` disk cache, then open `/model`.
match_rule: Must identify that `configured_standard_openrouter_profile_routes` only reads the `"openrouter"` disk cache namespace without triggering/scheduling any refresh, and when a direct profile owns the shared OpenRouter slot no active refresh path ever writes to the `"openrouter"` namespace, leaving standard OpenRouter models missing from `/model`.
near_misses: Complaining about `source_api_base` matching `openrouter.ai`, `is_listable_model_name` filtering, or env file parsing.
why_findable: Checking the cache writer in `crates/jcode-provider-openrouter/src/lib.rs` and `src/provider/openrouter.rs` shows refreshes only write to `configured_cache_namespace()`, so the new reader for the inactive `"openrouter"` namespace has no writer when a direct profile owns the slot.
notes: no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `CopilotApiProvider::stream_request` wraps `process_sse_stream(resp, tx.clone())` in a retry loop that continues to the next attempt on any retryable stream/timeout error while reusing the same `tx` channel without tracking whether partial output was already emitted or signaling a rollback. Because `process_sse_stream` forwards `TextDelta`/`ToolUseStart` events directly to `tx` as chunks arrive and `src/agent.rs` appends all stream events without clearing accumulators on `ConnectionPhase::Retrying`, a mid-stream timeout or error replays the response from the start and duplicates/garbles already-streamed output.
trigger: A Copilot SSE stream emits partial `TextDelta` or `ToolUseStart` events and then encounters a retryable stream error or chunk timeout (`Err(e)` from `process_sse_stream`).
match_rule: Must identify that retrying `process_sse_stream(resp, tx.clone())` after `process_sse_stream` has already emitted partial `StreamEvent`s (`TextDelta`/`ToolUseStart`) to `tx` replays the request onto the same event stream without rollback or guarding against post-output retries, causing the consumer (`agent.rs`/TUI) to duplicate/corrupt partial output.
near_misses: Discussing backoff duration, `MAX_RETRIES`, auth token refresh, or `is_retryable_error` substring patterns.
why_findable: `process_sse_stream` in the same file tracks `saw_any_data` only for logging and sends `TextDelta`/`ToolUseStart` straight to `tx`, while `src/agent.rs` blindly appends every `TextDelta`/`ToolUseStart` and does not reset on `ConnectionPhase::Retrying`.
notes: base = intro^. Fix ec2f3f84a3 wires shared attempt_tracker/RetryRollback into copilot.rs and all HTTP providers; its added tests are attempt_tracker.rs unit tests (tracker_forwards_in_order_and_reports_output) and openrouter_tests.rs::midstream_transport_fault_emits_retry_rollback_before_replay (no Copilot-specific test file). | no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `build_reasoning_request_parts_inner` filters `self.reasoning_effort()` with `.filter(|effort| *effort != "none")`, collapsing an explicit `"none"` effort into `None` (indistinguishable from unset effort). It then falls back to `show_thinking` (default `true`) and enables `ApiThinking::Adaptive` or `ApiThinking::Enabled` even when reasoning effort was explicitly disabled with `"none"`.
trigger: Configure `display.show_thinking = true` (the default) and set Anthropic reasoning effort explicitly to `"none"` (or use a model defaulting to `"none"`), then build a request.
match_rule: Must identify that filtering `"none"` to `None` before checking `show_thinking` in `build_reasoning_request_parts_inner` causes an explicit `effort = "none"` to still request adaptive or manual thinking whenever `show_thinking` is true.
near_misses: Discussing markdown emphasis latching, `output_config` omission, or manual thinking budget numbers.
why_findable: The `.filter(|effort| *effort != "none")` line sits directly above the new `(effort.is_some() || show_thinking)` and `effort.or(show_thinking.then_some("low"))` fallback in `build_reasoning_request_parts_inner`.

defect: `2b3c1dec8d` changed `/resume` session preview loading to run asynchronously (`pending_preview_load`), so the initial frame renders a short `"Loading…"` placeholder (`messages_preview` is empty and `max_scroll == 0`). However, `render_preview` unconditionally sets `self.scroll_offset = max_scroll; self.auto_scroll_preview = false;` on that placeholder frame, and `poll_pending_preview_load` never re-arms `auto_scroll_preview` when the real transcript arrives, leaving the preview pinned at the top instead of scrolling to the bottom (which also prevents the sticky prompt header from appearing).
trigger: Open `/resume` on a session whose transcript is loaded asynchronously so at least one frame renders while `pending_preview_load` is active and `messages_preview` is empty, then let the background preview load complete.
match_rule: Must identify that `render_preview` consumes `auto_scroll_preview = false` on the placeholder frame while `pending_preview_load` is still in flight (`messages_preview` empty / `max_scroll == 0`), and nothing re-arms `auto_scroll_preview` when the async preview finishes, leaving the loaded preview stuck at the top.
near_misses: Discussing preview search highlighting, session list loading placeholder, or wrapped line caching.
why_findable: The commit introduces `pending_preview_load` and leaves `messages_preview` empty until `poll_pending_preview_load` receives the background result, while `render_preview` in the same file clears `self.auto_scroll_preview = false` on every first render regardless of loading state.

defect: `bc8f284c91` changed `/rewind` and `/rewind N` in `commands.rs` to number and validate targets against `app.session.visible_conversation_message_count()` (excluding hidden `<system-reminder>` messages), rejecting any `N > visible_count`. However, `/rewind ` autocomplete in `state_ui_input_helpers.rs` was not updated and continued generating suggestions from `1..=self.session.messages.len()`, offering out-of-range rewind numbers that the command handler rejects.
trigger: Have a session containing at least one hidden `<system-reminder>` message and one visible message (`messages.len() > visible_conversation_message_count()`), then type `/rewind ` to trigger autocomplete.
match_rule: Must identify that after `/rewind` switched to `visible_conversation_message_count()` in `commands.rs`, the `/rewind ` autocomplete generator in `state_ui_input_helpers.rs` still iterates `1..=self.session.messages.len()`, suggesting invalid out-of-range rewind indices.
near_misses: Only mentioning fuzzy matching of `/rewind 10` -> `/rewind 1` (a separate pre-existing autocomplete issue), or remote rewind protocol serialization.
why_findable: The diff updates every `/rewind` length check in `commands.rs` from `self.session.messages.len()` to `visible_conversation_message_count()`, making the untouched `1..=self.session.messages.len()` in `state_ui_input_helpers.rs` immediately inconsistent.

defect: `OpenRouterProvider::context_window()` only consults the in-memory `self.models_cache` before falling back to static defaults, ignoring the persisted disk cache (`load_disk_cache()`). Because `OpenRouterProvider::new` initializes `models_cache` empty (`ModelsCache::default()`) and refreshes it asynchronously—unlike `models()` right above it which falls back to `load_disk_cache()`—fresh provider instances ignore persisted live `/models` `context_length` metadata and report wrong static fallback context limits.
trigger: Persist a model's live `context_length` to the OpenRouter disk cache, construct a fresh `OpenRouterProvider` (whose in-memory `models_cache` is still empty), and call `context_window()`.
match_rule: Must identify that `OpenRouterProvider::context_window()` only checks in-memory `self.models_cache` (initialized empty in `new()`) and falls back to static defaults without consulting the persisted disk cache (`load_disk_cache()`), losing live model context windows on fresh provider instances.
near_misses: Complaining about `try_read()` contention, hardcoded GPT-5.x fallback values in `provider/mod.rs`, or Codex API fetching.
why_findable: Literally 20 lines above the new `context_window()` method in `src/provider/openrouter.rs`, `models()` falls back to `load_disk_cache()` when `self.models_cache` is empty, and `OpenRouterProvider::new` initializes `models_cache` to `ModelsCache::default()`.
notes: fix_test corrected by audit: src/provider/openrouter_tests.rs::openai_compatible_model_catalog_refresh_calls_models_endpoint_and_updates_disk_cache names no test the fix adds that exercises the defect

defect: The TUI header auth-tag computation in `src/tui/ui.rs` lowercases `app.provider_name()` and matches `"anthropic" => { ... }` to display `oauth` or `api-key`. However, `MultiProvider::name()` in `src/provider/mod.rs` returns `"Claude"` (lowercased to `"claude"`) for `ActiveProvider::Claude`, so the `"anthropic"` match arm never matches and the Claude auth tag silently vanishes from the header.
trigger: Render the TUI header while running on `MultiProvider` with `ActiveProvider::Claude` and valid Anthropic OAuth or API-key credentials.
match_rule: Must identify the string mismatch between `src/tui/ui.rs` matching lowercased provider name `"anthropic"` and `MultiProvider::name()` returning `"Claude"` (`"claude"`), causing the auth tag for Claude/Anthropic sessions to always resolve to empty string.
near_misses: Complaining about OAuth vs API-key precedence order, OpenAI/Copilot tag strings, or Ctrl+C resume hints.
why_findable: Checking the producer of `app.provider_name()` (`MultiProvider::name()` in `src/provider/mod.rs:1668`) immediately shows it returns `"Claude"`, never `"anthropic"`.

defect: In Phase 1 of `calculate_placements_anchored`, when an anchored widget is temporarily covered (`hidden_frames <= MAX_HIDDEN_FRAMES`), it retains its slot in `next_anchors` so it will reappear there once unobstructed, but executes `continue` before the `all_rects` row-reservation loop. Phase 2 can then place a different widget into those unreserved rows; when the wide content scrolls past and the hidden anchor reappears, the two widgets overlap at the same screen rows.
trigger: Anchor widget A at rows R, scroll a wide line over R so A hides in place while another widget B is placed by Phase 2 onto rows R, then scroll past the wide line so A becomes visible again.
match_rule: Must identify that hidden-in-place anchors kept in `next_anchors` skip reserving/carving their rows out of `all_rects` (because of the early `continue`), allowing Phase 2 to place another widget in the same rows and causing overlap when the hidden widget returns.
near_misses: Complaining about `MAX_HIDDEN_FRAMES` constant, `WIDTH_GROW_HYSTERESIS`, or `overview_active` mergeable-widget suppression.
why_findable: The early `continue` for hidden-in-place anchors sits right above the `for rect in all_rects.iter_mut()` reservation loop in the same `calculate_placements_anchored` function.

defect: When serializing an assistant message that has only `Reasoning` blocks (no text and no tool calls, e.g. from an interrupted turn), `assistant_msg["reasoning_content"]` is only populated when `allow_reasoning` is true, yet the subsequent push guard `if !text_content.is_empty() || !tool_calls.is_empty() || has_reasoning_content` checks `has_reasoning_content` unconditionally. When `allow_reasoning` is false, this pushes a bare `{"role":"assistant"}` object with neither `content` nor `tool_calls`, which OpenAI-compatible APIs reject with HTTP 400 and permanently wedge the session.
trigger: Persist an assistant message containing only a `ContentBlock::Reasoning` block (empty text and no tool calls) and send the conversation to an OpenRouter/OpenAI-compatible provider with `allow_reasoning == false`.
match_rule: Must identify that adding `|| has_reasoning_content` to the `api_messages.push(assistant_msg)` guard without checking whether `reasoning_content` was actually attached (`allow_reasoning`) emits a bare `{"role":"assistant"}` message with no `content`, `tool_calls`, or `reasoning_content`.
near_misses: Complaining about Kimi headers, SSE `data:` parsing without space, or `" "` placeholder reasoning payload when `tool_calls` is non-empty.
why_findable: The `if allow_reasoning` block that conditionally sets `assistant_msg["reasoning_content"]` is immediately above the `if !text_content.is_empty() || !tool_calls.is_empty() || has_reasoning_content` guard in the diff.

defect: `InterruptSignal::notified(&self)` checks `if self.is_set() { return; }` and only afterwards calls `self.notify.notified().await`. Because `fire()` sets the `AtomicBool` and calls `notify_waiters()` (which does not store a permit for future waiters), a concurrent `fire()` between `is_set()` and `notified().await` drops the wakeup and hangs the waiter indefinitely.
trigger: Task A calls `signal.notified()`, sees `is_set() == false`, and before it polls `self.notify.notified()`, Task B calls `signal.fire()`; Task A then awaits `notify.notified()` forever.
match_rule: Must identify the lost-wakeup TOCTOU race in `InterruptSignal::notified()` where `is_set()` is checked before creating/registering the `tokio::sync::Notify::notified()` future (which must be created/pinned before checking the flag when paired with `notify_waiters()`).
near_misses: Discussing `Ordering::SeqCst` vs `Ordering::Acquire/Release`, or the reload `watch` channel in `server.rs`.
why_findable: `fire()` uses `notify_waiters()` (not `notify_one()`) right above `notified()` in the same 25-line `impl InterruptSignal` block, making the missing pre-check `notified()` registration immediately visible.
notes: no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `e4d3932a9a` adds a 5-minute client-side stream stall detector in `src/tui/app.rs` that auto-cancels processing whenever no `ServerEvent` arrives (`last_stream_activity`). However, `src/provider/anthropic.rs` silently drops SSE `"ping"` keepalive events (`// Keepalive, ignore`) and `src/agent.rs` emits no `ServerEvent` for `StreamEvent::ThinkingDelta` when `show_thinking` is off, so a healthy stream in a long extended-thinking phase produces zero client events and gets falsely auto-cancelled.
location: src/tui/app.rs (L530, L822, L4357), src/provider/anthropic.rs (L1068-1070), and src/agent.rs (L1883, L2590, L3245)
trigger: Run an Anthropic turn with `display.show_thinking = false` whose extended-thinking phase lasts longer than the 5-minute stall timeout while the provider streams `ThinkingDelta` and SSE `ping` keepalives.
match_rule: Must identify that the TUI stall auto-cancel relies solely on receiving `ServerEvent`s (`last_stream_activity`), while the provider/agent pipeline drops Anthropic `ping` keepalives and/or emits no `ServerEvent` during hidden `ThinkingDelta` reasoning phases, causing healthy long thinking phases to be falsely cancelled as stalled.
near_misses: Suggesting changing the 5-minute constant duration or complaining about disconnect reset logic.
why_findable: Tracing what `ServerEvent`s the server emits during an active provider stream in `src/provider/anthropic.rs:1068` (`"ping"` ignored) and `src/agent.rs` (`ThinkingDelta` hidden when `show_thinking` is false) shows zero events reach the TUI during silent reasoning.

defect: `spawn_resume_in_new_terminal_with_provider` and `spawn_selfdev_in_new_terminal_with_provider` pass the session/runtime `provider_key` verbatim as `--provider <provider_key>` when spawning a child `jcode` terminal process. However, persisted runtime provider keys use values like `"anthropic-api-key"`, `"claude-oauth"`, or `"openai-compatible:zai"`, whereas the CLI `--provider` flag is parsed by clap into `ProviderChoice` (`"anthropic-api"`, `"claude"`, `"openai"`, etc.), causing clap to reject the flag with exit code 2 and immediately kill the spawned window.
trigger: Spawn a visible swarm agent or resumed terminal window from a session whose `provider_key` is a runtime/auth key such as `"anthropic-api-key"` or `"claude-oauth"`.
match_rule: Must identify the vocabulary mismatch between the raw `provider_key` passed verbatim to `--provider` in `spawn_*_with_provider` and the valid CLI `ProviderChoice` enum values accepted by `--provider`, causing spawned child `jcode` processes to fail argument parsing.
near_misses: Complaining about terminal emulator quoting, `--fresh-spawn` flag ordering, or `try_lock()` failure when reading coordinator identity.
why_findable: Inspecting `--provider` in `src/cli/args.rs` / `ProviderChoice` alongside the session `provider_key` values shows `provider_key` uses runtime/auth identifiers that are not valid `ProviderChoice` CLI values.

defect: `App::handle_login_completed` runs synchronously on the TUI event loop and directly invokes `self.provider.on_auth_changed()`. In the same commit, `MultiProvider::on_auth_changed()` performs synchronous `AuthStatus::check()` (filesystem probes and subprocesses) and `CopilotApiProvider::new()` under RwLock, blocking and freezing the TUI event/render loop on login completion.
trigger: Complete an in-TUI provider login so `BusEvent::LoginCompleted { success: true }` is handled by `App::handle_login_completed` on the TUI main loop.
match_rule: Must identify that calling `self.provider.on_auth_changed()` synchronously inside `App::handle_login_completed` blocks the TUI event/render loop because `MultiProvider::on_auth_changed()` performs synchronous credential probing (`AuthStatus::check()`) and provider initialization (`CopilotApiProvider::new()`).
near_misses: Complaining about `copilot_api.read().unwrap()` poison handling or selfdev reload signaling.
why_findable: Both the synchronous call site in `src/tui/app.rs` (`handle_login_completed`) and the blocking `MultiProvider::on_auth_changed()` implementation are added in the same small commit.

defect: `summarize_model_catalog_refresh` computes `routes_changed` by comparing `(route.available, route.detail, estimated_cost)` verbatim between `before_routes` and `after_routes`. Because provider route builders embed relative display-only cache-age suffixes (such as `"5m ago"`, `"2h ago"`) inside `route.detail`, refreshing the model catalog causes unchanged routes whose age text ticked to be spuriously counted as changed routes.
trigger: Run `/refresh-model-list` when `before_routes` has `detail: "..., 5m ago"` and `after_routes` has the exact same route with `detail: "..., 0m ago"` or empty age suffix.
match_rule: Must identify that `summarize_model_catalog_refresh` compares raw `route.detail` strings without stripping/normalizing display-only relative age suffixes (e.g. `"5m ago"`, `"2h ago"`) produced in `ModelRoute.detail`, causing unchanged routes to inflate `routes_changed`.
near_misses: Complaining about `estimated_reference_cost_micros` precision, `BTreeSet` ordering, or Antigravity `api_method` naming.
why_findable: Checking what `MultiProvider::model_routes` / `openrouter.rs` places in `ModelRoute.detail` shows relative cache-age strings like `"Nm ago"` that inevitably change across any refresh.

defect: `is_retryable_error` checks `error_str.contains("5") && (error_str.contains("50") || error_str.contains("502") || ...)` without checking the actual HTTP status code. Any deterministic 4xx client error (such as HTTP 402 Payment Required or 400 Bad Request) whose response body happens to contain the digits `"50"` (for example a token count like `"500"` or `"15000"`) is misclassified as a retryable 5xx server error and retried needlessly.
trigger: Receive an HTTP 402 or 400 error from OpenRouter whose JSON error body contains the substring `"50"` (e.g. a token budget number).
match_rule: Must identify that `error_str.contains("50")` in `openrouter.rs::is_retryable_error` is an overly loose substring check that matches arbitrary numbers containing `"50"` in non-retryable 4xx error bodies (instead of parsing/checking the HTTP status code or excluding 4xx client errors).
near_misses: Complaining about `"eof"` matching words containing `eof`, backoff timing, or Anthropic/OpenAI retry classifiers.
why_findable: `error_str.contains("50")` is right inside the new `is_retryable_error` function in `src/provider/openrouter.rs` and obviously subsumes `502`/`503`/`504` and matches any `50` digits anywhere in the formatted HTTP response body.
notes: no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `spawn_swarm_agent` computes `let spawn_model = coordinator_model.or(configured_swarm_model);` and `let spawn_provider_key = coordinator_provider_key.or_else(...)`. Because `coordinator_model` is the coordinator's active model (`Some(...)`), it always shadows the user's explicit `agents.swarm_model` configuration, and even when `configured_swarm_model` is used, blindly preferring `coordinator_provider_key` pairs the configured swarm model with the coordinator's provider key instead of the provider for that model.
trigger: Configure `agents.swarm_model` in config to a model different from the coordinator's active model and spawn a swarm agent.
match_rule: Must identify that `coordinator_model.or(configured_swarm_model)` gives the coordinator's model precedence over `agents.swarm_model` (so configured `swarm_model` is ignored whenever `coordinator_model` is `Some`), and/or that `coordinator_provider_key` is inherited even when `spawn_model` comes from `configured_swarm_model`.
near_misses: Discussing `try_lock()` contention on the coordinator mutex, or CLI `--provider` vocabulary validation.
why_findable: The two lines `let configured_swarm_model = ...; let spawn_model = coordinator_model.or(configured_swarm_model);` immediately show `configured_swarm_model` is only used as a fallback behind `coordinator_model`, inverting config override precedence.

defect: The `/rewind N` handler truncates `self.session.messages` and rebuilds `display_messages`, and sets `self.provider_session_id = None`, but never truncates `self.messages` (the active provider message vector passed to `self.provider.complete(&self.messages, ...)` on subsequent turns) and never clears `self.session.provider_session_id` before saving. As a result, the TUI looks rewound while the next LLM turn still sends all the rewound messages to the provider.
trigger: Send 3 messages in a local TUI session, execute `/rewind 2`, and inspect `app.messages` or send another prompt to the provider.
match_rule: Must identify that `/rewind N` truncates `self.session.messages` and rebuilds `display_messages` but fails to truncate/rebuild `self.messages` (the provider conversation history sent by `run_turn`), and/or fails to clear `self.session.provider_session_id` before `self.session.save()`.
near_misses: Complaining about 1-based vs 0-based indexing, missing `/rewind` undo, or hidden `<system-reminder>` messages.
why_findable: Checking `/clear` and `run_turn` in `src/tui/app.rs` shows `self.messages` is the separate provider message buffer sent to `provider.complete(...)`, which `/clear` clears alongside `self.session.messages` while `/rewind N` forgets to update it.

defect: `fc23734102` added Anthropic cost estimation in `App::update_cost_impl` using `full_input_tokens = self.streaming_input_tokens.saturating_sub(cache_read_tokens.min(self.streaming_input_tokens))` and omitting `streaming_cache_creation_tokens` entirely. In Anthropic's split token accounting (as reported by `anthropic.rs` and already handled in `effective_context_tokens_from_usage`), `input_tokens` already excludes `cache_read` and `cache_creation`, so subtracting `cache_read_tokens` double-subtracts cache reads (billing fresh input near $0 on cache hits) and fails to bill cache-creation writes.

notes: no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `handle_http` performs a single `tcp_stream.read(&mut buf).await?` and immediately parses the HTTP headers and JSON body from `&buf[..n]`. When an HTTP client (such as iOS `URLSession`) transmits the POST `/pair` headers and body in separate TCP segments, the first `read()` returns only the headers with an empty body, causing `/pair` to reject valid pairing requests.
trigger: Send a `POST /pair` HTTP request where the headers and JSON body arrive in separate TCP segments.
match_rule: Must identify that `handle_http` does only a single `tcp_stream.read` instead of looping until the `\r\n\r\n` header terminator and full `Content-Length` body bytes have been read.
near_misses: Complaining about the 8192-byte buffer size or CORS headers without identifying the single `read()` dropping split TCP segments.
why_findable: Directly visible in `handle_http`: one `let n = tcp_stream.read(&mut buf).await?;` call followed immediately by splitting headers and body on `\r\n\r\n`.
notes: base = intro^. Local single-function framing bug (relation: false). | no_regression_test: the fix commit adds or changes no test that exercises the defect (fix_test audit)

defect: `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point` widened the edge auto-scroll trigger into a multi-row hot zone (`row <= area.y + zone` / `row >= last_row - zone`, up to 3 rows inside the pane) without checking whether the pane can actually scroll (`snapshot.scroll > 0` or `snapshot.visible_end < snapshot.wrapped_plain_line_count()`). Because `copy_selection.rs:518-524` calls `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point` ahead of normal in-pane cell selection and immediately snaps the selection to `edge_point` (`last_row`/`area.y`) and returns early, dragging into the bottom 3 rows while pinned at the bottom (the default view) snaps the selection to the very last row and prevents selecting text in those rows.

match_rule: Must connect `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point` matching the multi-row top/bottom hot zone unconditionally (even when the pane cannot scroll further up/down) to `copy_selection.rs` prioritizing it over normal cell hit-testing and snapping the selection to `area.y`/`last_row`.
near_misses: Complaining about `edge_autoscroll_zone_rows` formula on tiny panes or horizontal column clamping without identifying the missing can-scroll check when already pinned at top/bottom.
why_findable: The diff expands `row >= last_row` to `row >= last_row - zone` (up to 3 rows into content) inside `copy_pane_vertical_edge_point`, while its caller in `copy_selection.rs:518-524` invokes it before in-pane cell selection and short-circuits with `update_selection_with_point(edge_point, true)` and `return Some(false)`.
notes: base = intro^. Distinct intro b58bed9b12 (25 lines); 4faab84671 is the intro of order_index 0.

defect: `refresh_runtime_handles(agent)` unconditionally awaits `agent.lock().await` to re-clone `(soft_interrupt_queue, background_tool_signal, cancel_signal)` during `ResumeSession` (line 656) and `Subscribe` (line 850). However, active turn execution holds `agent.lock().await` for the entire streaming turn (which is why those signals are also tracked lock-free in `shutdown_signals` and `soft_interrupt_queues`). When a client reconnects to a busy session, `refresh_runtime_handles(&agent).await` stalls the client's control loop until the turn finishes, making cancel/interrupt requests unresponsive during the turn.
trigger: A client reconnects (`ResumeSession` / `Subscribe`) to a session whose `Agent` mutex is currently held by an in-progress streaming turn and tries to cancel or soft-interrupt it.
match_rule: Must connect `refresh_runtime_handles` calling `agent.lock().await` on reconnect/subscribe to active turn execution holding `agent`'s mutex for the duration of a turn, blocking the client connection from obtaining cancel/interrupt control handles (despite lock-free `shutdown_signals`/`soft_interrupt_queues` registries).
near_misses: Complaining about `sessions.read()` RwLock contention or `Subscribe` snapshot locking without identifying `refresh_runtime_handles` blocking on `agent.lock().await`.
why_findable: The diff adds `refresh_runtime_handles` calling `agent.lock().await` and invokes it on `ResumeSession` and `Subscribe` in the same `handle_client` function that explicitly comments (lines 162-178) that interrupt/cancel handles are fetched lock-free because `Agent` is locked while processing.

defect: In the detached-turn cancel path (`else` branch of `cancel_processing_message` when no local `turn_task` exists), `972cab06ed` calls `session_control.request_cancel()` (firing the shared `InterruptSignal`) and spawns a background task that sleeps 500ms and then unconditionally calls `reset_control.reset_cancel()` (clearing the `AtomicBool` flag). If a second cancel arrives within that 500ms window (e.g., rapid Esc presses), the first cancel's stale 500ms timer fires and clears the `InterruptSignal` before the running turn observes the newer cancel, silently dropping the interrupt.
trigger: Send two `Cancel` requests less than 500ms apart on a reconnected/detached busy session (no local processing task); the first task's 500ms timer resets the shared `InterruptSignal` right after the second cancel fires it.
match_rule: Must identify that the spawned 500ms sleep task unconditionally calls `reset_cancel()` on the shared `InterruptSignal` without checking whether a newer cancel/fire occurred in the meantime (e.g. via an epoch/generation counter), erasing a subsequent cancel within the 500ms window.
near_misses: Complaining only about the 500ms duration being too short/long or about `handle.abort()` in the local-task branch without identifying the stale deferred `reset_cancel()` clearing a newer `request_cancel()`.
why_findable: The diff adds `session_control.request_cancel()` followed by `tokio::spawn(async move { sleep(500ms).await; reset_control.reset_cancel(); })` where `SessionControlHandle::request_cancel`/`reset_cancel` operate directly on a single boolean `InterruptSignal` without any generation/epoch check.
notes: base = intro^. 972cab06ed is the fix commit of order_index 107; this defect is specifically in the new detached-cancel branch introduced by 972cab06ed.

defect: `bc8f284c91` added remote `/rewind` where the client (`remote_rewindable_messages` in `src/tui/app/remote/key_handling.rs`) numbers and validates targets against `app.display_messages()` filtered to `role == "user" | "assistant"` (populated from `render_messages` in `src/session/render.rs`, which omits tool-call-only assistant messages and renders `ToolResult` messages with `role == "tool"`). On the server, however, `Agent::rewind_to_message` (`src/agent/turn_execution.rs`) resolves the 1-based `message_index` via `Session::stored_len_for_visible_conversation_message` (`src/session.rs`), whose `is_visible_conversation_message` predicate only skips `display_role.is_some()` and `<system-reminder>` messages and still counts raw `ToolUse`-only assistant messages and `ToolResult`-only user messages. In any tool-using session, remote `/rewind N` truncates to a much earlier stored message than entry `N` shown by `/rewind`.
trigger: In a remote session with tool calls (e.g., Turn 1 prompt -> assistant `ToolUse`-only message -> user `ToolResult` message -> assistant text answer, then Turn 2 prompt -> assistant text answer), run `/rewind` (showing 4 rendered entries: 1 prompt-1, 2 answer-1, 3 prompt-2, 4 answer-2) and then `/rewind 3`; `Agent::rewind_to_message(3)` maps 3 to stored length 3 (mid-turn after `ToolResult`) instead of stored length 5 (`prompt-2`).

near_misses: Only noting that `/rewind ` autocomplete in `state_ui_input_helpers.rs` uses `self.session.messages.len()` (separate defect already admitted at [20] on the same commit), or commenting only on `<system-reminder>` text matching or `Request::Rewind` JSON serialization without identifying the tool-call/tool-result count divergence between rendered transcript entries and `is_visible_conversation_message`.
why_findable: The diff introduces both sides of the mismatch (`remote_rewindable_messages` filtering `display_messages()` to `"user" | "assistant"` and `Agent::rewind_to_message` -> `is_visible_conversation_message` over `session.messages`) plus `handle_get_history` right after rewind. Inspecting `src/session/render.rs:render_messages_and_images_with_compacted_history` (which builds `display_messages`) shows that `ToolUse`-only assistant messages emit no `"assistant"` entry (`!text.is_empty()` is false) and `ToolResult` user messages emit `role: "tool"`, immediately disagreeing with `is_visible_conversation_message`.
notes: Shares already-confirmed intro_commit bc8f284c91 with [20] rewind-autocomplete-uses-raw-message-count; distinct defect (remote /rewind client-vs-server rendered-vs-stored index mismatch vs autocomplete raw messages.len() for <system-reminder>). Fix commit afe1fd540c (issue #432) adds stored_index to RenderedMessage and Session::rewind_target_stored_indices()/rewind_target_count() and updates Agent::rewind_to_message, local /rewind, and autocomplete.

defect: `c2974ee8e6` adds selectable slash-command suggestions (`command_suggestion_selected`, `move_command_suggestion_selection`, `accept_selected_command_suggestion`, and the highlighted `▸` row in `src/tui/ui_input.rs`) and initializes `command_suggestion_selected: 0` in both local and remote `App` constructors (`tui_lifecycle.rs:516,884`).
